//: The reviewed size of this package's surface: what a reader has to hold in
their head, counted the way `scripts/check-complexity.ts` counts it.
Limits are the exact current numbers, with no headroom on purpose. Byte
budgets carry ~1 % because compression is not byte-stable; a count is, and
headroom here would just be room to grow into without saying so. Raising a
number is a two-line change: the number, and why it moved.

publicDeclarations.why: Every exported name across all API reports. The number a consumer's editor offers them, and the number this package has to keep meaning something. 2026-09-06: +12 for the two zero-config setups — `withLivePreview()` for Next.js and the Nuxt module — which exist to remove lines from a consumer's project, not to add names to it. +5 for asset delivery: a route factory in each of the three adapters, plus what a route file re-exports in the two that name it. +13 for the build-time annotator, nine of them its own entry. 2026-09-06 (1.x-Upgrade): +1, `isPreviewRequest` back as a deprecated alias — measured against the published 1.8.1 surface, it is the only renamed function among the eight names that left, and the alias is what makes a 1.x project compile against 2.0 unchanged. 2026-09-06 (R9): −5, two concepts with no remaining reason — `PreviewBindingsCommonOptions`, a one-member base left behind when its sibling options type was removed in 2.0, and `AnnotatableEntry`, which had one member and one use. 2026-09-07 (Z6): +14 across five reports, and they are four names, not fourteen — `registerRouteRefresh` and its `RouteRefresh` on the root, core, client and react entries, `RouteOutcome` on the five that name `RouteStrategy`, and `LivePreviewRouteRefresh` with its props on `./react` alone. One concept: the host framework re-renders its own route instead of this package morphing fetched HTML over the reconciler's nodes. 2026-09-07 (Z8): +3 on `./nextjs` alone — `LivePreviewScript`, `LivePreviewScriptComponentProps`, `LivePreviewScriptElement`. One concept again: the script as something a server component decides to render, rather than something a synchronous helper builds for whoever asks. It is the only delivery in the package that can charge a public visitor nothing on a framework whose middleware cannot inject into a body.

entrySubpaths.why: Import specifiers in the manifest. Each one is a decision a reader makes before writing a line of code, so a new entry needs a reason a sentence can hold. 2026-09-06: +1 for `./nuxt-module`, which Nuxt loads by specifier from `modules: []` and so cannot live behind an existing entry. +1 for `./annotate`, which is separate so a build plugin does not drag `ts-morph` into a project.

adapterOptions.why: Members of `PreviewAdapterOptions`: what every adapter takes. The single most-read type in the package. 2026-09-06: +2, `delivery` and `assetPath` — one concept, but the second is the path both halves must agree on, and folding it into the first would hide that. 2026-09-07: +1, `onUnfaithfulPatch` — the renamed `onUnboundChange`, which stays beside it as a deprecated alias until 3.0. The two are one decision, so this is a name a reader meets twice, not a second thing to understand; the alias goes and the count returns to 32. 2026-09-10 (Z9): +1, `autoBind` — the one option that changes what a page needs in its markup, and therefore one every adapter has to be able to say, because the adapter is where a project that wants no attributes configures the runtime.

inlineOptions.why: Members of `InlineScriptConfig`: what the generated script carries. Most of them travel in the positional wire tuple, which is append-only. 2026-09-07: +1, `onUnfaithfulPatch` — its own slot rather than a widened `onUnboundChange`, because the tuple is append-only in both directions: a 2.0 page whose script is already on a CDN keeps writing `'route'` into slot 20 and must keep meaning `'escalate'` by it. 2026-09-10 (Z9): +1, `autoBind`, slot 22 — an omitted slot reads as `'off'`, so a script generated before the option existed keeps meaning what it meant.

diagnosticCodes.why: LP codes. A code is a promise to explain one situation; forty is a table someone can skim, and a hundred would be a table nobody reads. 2026-09-06: +1 for LP0409, the strict sanitizer reporting an attribute the 1.x default kept — the one 2.0 behaviour change an upgrading project could otherwise only discover by looking. 2026-09-07: +1 for LP0410, a Lexical block with no renderer — the preview now keeps the server's markup for it instead of writing an empty placeholder over it, and a reader who sees an unrendered block needs to be told which slug to register rather than left to compare two page sources. 2026-09-07: +1 for LP0411, a patch the runtime knows cannot match the server's render. It is one code for every reason a patch falls short, because the reader's question is the same in all of them — why did my page reload, or why is this field not what the server shows — and the answer is one sentence plus the field's name. 2026-09-10: +1 for LP0412, the first write to a date, number or checkbox binding replacing a different reading of the same value. It is a separate code from LP0411 because it is a separate situation: LP0411 is a patch that could not be made, this is a patch that was made and still left the page unlike the server's. The reader's question is different too — not "why did my page reload" but "why does this date look different than it did a second ago" — and so is the answer, which is one attribute in their own markup.

sourceModules.why: Source modules in the architecture graph. Files stay under 500 lines, so this is the other half of that rule: many small files are only better than few large ones while the count itself stays legible. 2026-09-06: +2, the Nuxt module and the Next.js config wrapper; +2, the shared runtime-asset descriptor and the Next.js asset route; +2, the SvelteKit and Nuxt ones; +2, the annotator plugin and its entry; +1, the sanitizer's upgrade report. 2026-09-07: +1, the relationship tracker — reading `externallyUpdatedRelationship` as an edge has two halves (has the event changed, does it name another document) and holds state between messages, so it is a named module beside the other trackers rather than a paragraph inside the pipeline. 2026-09-07: +1, the fidelity verdict — three places decide that a patch cannot reach the server's render (the writer, the rich-text renderer, the strategy runner) and one place has to hold the policy they share, or the option's meaning is spread across three files that cannot see each other. 2026-09-07: +1, the merge decision — whether a message needs the server at all is asked from the binding cache, the raw diff and the last resolved document at once, and it holds the window a burst of requests shares, so it is a module beside the merger it rations rather than three conditions inside the pipeline. 2026-09-07 (Z6): +2. `src/core/route-refresh.ts` is the seam between a host router and the route strategy — the strategy is built by an inline script before any component has mounted, so the two can only meet at a named slot, and the module is where that name and its two directions are written down once. `src/adapters/react/route-refresh.ts` is the component that writes it, which cannot live in the hook's file because it is a different job with a different lifetime. 2026-09-07 (Z8): +1, `src/adapters/nextjs/script-component.ts`. It is the only delivery in this package that can decline to render, and it is a React component rather than a function that returns a string, so it cannot live in `adapter.ts` beside the two synchronous helpers it exists to replace: different shape, different peer (`react`, loaded lazily), different answer to the same question. 2026-09-10 (Z9): +2. `src/core/auto-bind.ts` is the search, its exclusions and the candidate rule — the one place in the package whose correctness is statistical rather than declared (ADR 0014), which is reason enough for it to be a file a reader can audit on its own. `src/core/transform-value.ts` is the plugin boundary on a value's way to its binding, moved out of the update pipeline because the pipeline reached the 500-line limit with the auto-binding hook and the transform is the one block in it that is about consumer code rather than about the update.

payload-live-preview.api.md.why: The root barrel: the client, the generator, the renderers, the DSL and the plugin surface in one import. The largest number here on purpose — and the one to watch, because every entry below re-exports from it. 2026-09-07 (Z6): +3 for the route-refresh seam.

payload-live-preview--core.api.md.why: The runtime without the generator and the built-in plugins. 2026-09-07 (Z6): +3 for the route-refresh seam — `registerRouteRefresh`, `RouteRefresh`, `RouteOutcome`.

payload-live-preview--server.api.md.why: Everything a server decides with: authorization, tokens, document reads, gated bindings, and reading a verdict back off locals.

payload-live-preview--client.api.md.why: `LivePreviewClient` and what its options and events name. 2026-09-07 (Z6): +3 for the route-refresh seam it shares with the root and core entries.

payload-live-preview--plugins.api.md.why: The manager, the contract and the built-in plugins.

payload-live-preview--fragment.api.md.why: The browser half of the fragment and route strategies. 2026-09-07 (Z6): +1, `RouteOutcome`, which this entry's `RouteStrategy` names in its own signature and would otherwise leave forgotten.

payload-live-preview--structural.api.md.why: The keyed morph and the structural array renderer.

payload-live-preview--codegen.api.md.why: Type generation and the annotate surface, including the schema shape the annotator reads.

payload-live-preview--astro.api.md.why: The integration, the middleware and the fragment endpoint.

payload-live-preview--nextjs.api.md.why: The middleware, the script props, the fragment endpoint, `withLivePreview()` for next.config.ts, and the runtime asset route. 2026-09-07 (Z8): +3, `LivePreviewScript` with the props it takes and the element it resolves to — the async server component that renders nothing for a request without an authorization verdict. One concept, and the two types beside it exist so a JSX consumer can name what it hands over and what comes back without this entry importing React's types.

payload-live-preview--lexical.api.md.why: The Lexical renderer and its node registry.

payload-live-preview--nuxt.api.md.why: The Nitro plugin, the handler, the fragment endpoint and the runtime asset route.

payload-live-preview--doctor.api.md.why: `runDoctor()` and the probe analysis as a library.

payload-live-preview--sveltekit.api.md.why: The handle, the fragment endpoint and the runtime asset route.

payload-live-preview--annotate.api.md.why: The build-time annotator: the plugin, the transform behind it, and the schema shape it reads. No ts-morph, which is why it is not part of `./codegen`.

payload-live-preview--nuxt-module.api.md.why: The Nuxt module and the shapes it duck-types off Nuxt, so the package does not depend on `nuxt` to adapt it.

payload-live-preview--vue.api.md.why: The composable, its options and the four refs it returns.

payload-live-preview--react.api.md.why: The hook, its options and the snapshot it returns. 2026-09-07 (Z6): +4, `<LivePreviewRouteRefresh />` and its props plus the `registerRouteRefresh` seam it re-exports — the entry now has a second job, and it is the one that keeps the route strategy off React's own DOM.

payload-live-preview--codegen--astro.api.why: The Astro integration that runs type generation on start and in dev.

payload-live-preview--lean.api.md.why: The lean runtime artifact as a value, and the type that describes one.

payload-live-preview--astro--middleware-.why: The entry the Astro integration registers as middleware; it reads its options from a virtual module.
